A neighbourhood table, done properly

Cafe Hiyam sits in the heart of Naval Anchorage, serving the families and food lovers of the area the food they grew up with — smoky BBQ straight off the coals and slow-cooked desi classics made fresh through the day.

There is no shortcut in the kitchen here. Meats are marinated before they ever meet the grill, karahis are cooked to order in the wok, and the chai is brewed the slow way — strong, milky and properly karak. Come in for a full family dinner, or just settle in with a cup of tea.

From the grill & the kitchen

The menu leans on two things Cafe Hiyam does best: charcoal BBQ and homestyle desi cooking.

Charcoal BBQ

Skewers of marinated chicken and minced meat grilled over live coals until the edges char and the inside stays juicy — served sizzling with lemon, onions and green chutney.

Karahis, cooked to order

The desi heart of the menu: chicken and meat tossed in the wok with tomato, green chillies, ginger and crushed spices, finished with fresh coriander and brought to the table still bubbling.

Rice, breads & the full spread

Fragrant layered rice, soft naan and roti from the tandoor, cool raita and crisp salads — everything you need to turn a grill platter into a proper feast for the whole table.

Chai & the cafe corner

Slow-brewed doodh patti, poured strong and milky, for the long conversations. Whether it rounds off a BBQ dinner or starts a slow morning, the kettle is always on.

The kitchen cooks in small batches and the selection changes through the day.
